data.name: Ephraim
data.long_meaning: In the Hebrew Bible, Ephraim is a son of Joseph and Asenath, born in Egypt. The name means 'son of fruitfulness' or 'fertile'. Ephraim is also one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

in_hebrew.name: אפרים
in_hebrew.meaning: משמעות שם: פרה ועדיה, בעברית, תיאור גאולה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שמו 'אפרים' נגזר מהמילה 'אפר', שפירושה 'פרה' או 'ניצוץ' (שמות 46:13) וגם 'עדיה', שפירושה 'אל-אדון' (יחזקאל 23:8) ובאחד מהמקראות 'עד', שפירושה 'עד' (בראשית 49:20).

in_english.name: Ephraim
in_english.meaning: name meaning: fruitful and famous, derived from Hebrew roots
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ephraim is derived from the Hebrew roots 'apar', meaning 'fruitful' and 'famous' (Genesis 46:13), and 'edia', meaning 'famous' and 'blessed' (Isaiah 23:8).

biblical_reference.note: Name of one of the sons of Joseph (Gen 46:13) and a tribe in the Old Testament.

saint_reference.note: Early Christian theologian, writer, and poet, known for his hymns and writings on spiritual growth.

data.cultural_impact: Ephraim has had a significant impact on Jewish and Christian history. It was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and the northern kingdom of Israel was named after it. The Wanderjahre (Years of Wandering) of the Hebrews after the exodus from Egypt were depicted in a song that referred to Ephraim and Manasseh, Joseph's sons, as 'Joseph's two sons, who became two nations.' Ephraim came to represent the Northern Kingdom of Israel in contrast to Judah, which represented the Southern Kingdom, commonly known as Judea.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Ephraim' comes from the Hebrew word meaning 'son of fruitfulness' or 'fertile'. This can be seen as a reference to God's provision and care for His people. In the book of Genesis, when Jacob blessed his grandsons, Ephraim and Manasseh, he placed his right hand on Ephraim's head, declaring that 'God make you fruitful and increase you, and make you a multitude of people.' This blessing reflected God's promise to bless His people and make them fruitful, a theme that runs throughout the Bible. Additionally, as the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel, Ephraim represents the fruitfulness and blessings that come from God's promise to make Israel a great nation.

historical_references.context: Ephraim is a biblical figure and the second son of Joseph and his wife Asenath, and the name is also associated with the northern kingdom of Israel in the Hebrew Bible.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Ephraim: Son of Joseph in the Old Testament, representing the northern kingdom of Israel. Symbolizes the wild and fruitful nature of God's people, with a tendency to wander and turn away from Him. Spiritually, it is a reminder to stay connected to God, as the ancient Israelites did through their faith and obedience.
